chunks: Certainly, if Allah were to allow anyone to indulge in pride, He would have allowed it to His selected prophets [and vicegerents],
But Allah, the Sublime, disliked vanity for them and liked humbleness for them.
Therefore, they laid their cheeks on the ground, smeared their faces with dust, bent themselves down for the believers, and remained humble people.
Allah tried them with hunger, afflicted them with difficulty, tested them with fear, and upset them with troubles.

key_terms.خَفَضُوا أَجْنِحَتَهُمْ: Bent their wings (metaphor for gentleness and submission)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between pride and humility in the context of prophets and saints according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) establishes that if God had permitted arrogance, He would have granted it to the prophets and saints, yet He chose humility for them as a divine preference. This passage underscores the Shia concept of *tawadu'* not merely as a virtue but as a tested state of being, where prophets and saints endured hunger, fatigue, and fear to demonstrate their submission. Their physical prostration and gentle demeanor towards believers serve as the ultimate model for the faithful, contrasting with the vanity of Satan.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Certainly, if Allāh were to allow anyone to indulge in pride He would have allowed it to his selected prophets and vicegerents.
